text: Given a tool call carries a valid X-PagerDuty-Api-Key header, when the tool calls PagerDuty, then the upstream request carries Authorization: Token token=<that key> and the tool returns PagerDuty's data.
evidence: uv run pytest -v tests/test_middleware.py::test_api_key_header_is_forwarded_as_authorization_token -> PASSED (full suite run 2026-10-30: 45 passed in 7.52s)

text: Given X-PagerDuty-Api-Key is missing, when any read tool is called, then the server responds 401 listing the missing header, and no call is made to PagerDuty.
evidence: uv run pytest -v tests/test_middleware.py::test_missing_api_key_is_401_with_no_upstream_call -> PASSED. Live curl confirms: POST /mcp with no headers -> HTTP 401, body {"error":"Missing credentials","message":"Missing PagerDuty headers: X-PagerDuty-Api-Key.","required_headers":["X-PagerDuty-Api-Key"],...}

text: Given X-PagerDuty-Api-Key is present but X-PagerDuty-From-Email is missing, when a write tool (e.g. pagerduty_incidents_update) is called, then the server responds 401 listing the missing header, and no call is made to PagerDuty.
evidence: uv run pytest -v tests/test_middleware.py -k from_email -> 5 PASSED; tests/test_records.py::test_write_tool_without_from_email_never_calls_pagerduty -> PASSED, asserts respx route.call_count == 0

text: Given incidents exist, when pagerduty_incidents_list is called with no filters, then it returns items/count/limit/offset/has_more (and next_offset when has_more is true).
Given pagerduty_incidents_list is called with limit=500, when the request is built, then the limit sent to PagerDuty is capped at 100, not passed through unbounded.
evidence: uv run pytest -v tests/test_handlers.py::test_incidents_list_limit_is_capped_at_100 -> PASSED. Note: implemented in tests/test_handlers.py, not the tests/test_argument_errors.py path originally sketched in this ledger -- no such file was created (the Tech design's Change list names only test_tools.py/test_middleware.py/test_handlers.py/test_records.py); the planned path above is corrected here, this is a test-location detail, not a change to what TC5 asserts.

text: Given an incident id that exists, when pagerduty_incidents_get is called with include_notes=true, then the response includes the incident's core fields plus its notes.
Given an incident id that does not exist, when pagerduty_incidents_get is called, then the tool returns a not_found envelope naming that id.
Given a valid service_id and a title, when pagerduty_incidents_create is called, then PagerDuty triggers a new incident on that service and the tool returns the created incident including its new id.
evidence: uv run pytest -v tests/test_handlers.py::test_incidents_create_triggers_new_incident -> PASSED; also asserts the From header is forwarded on the write call

text: Given an open incident id, when pagerduty_incidents_update is called with status="acknowledged", then the incident's status becomes acknowledged in the tool's response.
Given an incident already in status "acknowledged", when pagerduty_incidents_update is called again with status="acknowledged", then the call succeeds as a no-op and the returned status is unchanged.

Given an existing incident id and a target assignee user id, when pagerduty_incidents_update is called with assignee_user_ids=[that id], then PagerDuty reassigns the incident and the tool's response reflects the new assignee.

Given an existing incident id and note text, when pagerduty_incidents_add_note is called, then a follow-up pagerduty_incidents_get(include_notes=true) shows that note (id, content, author, timestamp) on the incident's timeline.
evidence: uv run pytest -v tests/test_handlers.py::test_incidents_add_note_appears_on_incident_timeline -> PASSED (asserts the note tool's own response shape directly; TC6 covers the get(include_notes=true) read-back path)

text: Given escalation policies exist, when pagerduty_escalation_policies_list/_get is called, then the policy's escalation rules and targets are returned, and no update/delete tool exists for this resource in the published tool table.
Given an existing on-call schedule, when pagerduty_schedules_get is called, then its layers and time zone are returned, and no update/delete tool exists for schedules in the published tool table.
Given on-call assignments exist for the current time, when pagerduty_oncalls_list is called with no time window (defaults to now) and no filters, then the currently on-call user(s) are returned.
evidence: uv run pytest -v tests/test_handlers.py::test_oncalls_list_defaults_to_now -> PASSED; asserts no since/until are sent to PagerDuty, which defaults to "now" per its own API

text: Given a resolved incident, when pagerduty_incident_reviews_create is called for it and then pagerduty_incident_reviews_get(include_action_items=true) is called on the result, then the created review is returned together with its action items (possibly an empty list).

Given PagerDuty responds 429 with a Retry-After header, when any tool calls it, then the tool returns {"error": {"code": "rate_limited", "retryable": true, ...}} after respecting the documented single-call retry budget, not an unhandled exception.
evidence: uv run pytest -v tests/test_records.py::test_429_maps_to_rate_limited_and_respects_retry_after -> PASSED; asserts exactly 3 upstream calls (initial + max_retries=2) before giving up and returning the envelope

text: Given PagerDuty responds 500, when any tool calls it, then the tool returns {"error": {"code": "upstream_error", "retryable": true, ...}}, never a raw 500 to the caller.

Given two concurrent requests carry two different X-PagerDuty-Api-Key values, when both call the same tool at the same time, then each request's outbound PagerDuty call uses only the key sent on that request, with no response or cached state leaking between them.
evidence: uv run pytest -v tests/test_middleware.py::test_concurrent_requests_do_not_leak_credentials_across_tenants -> PASSED (asyncio.gather of two tasks, each asserting it only ever observes its own contextvar-scoped api key)

text: Given this connector is registered on the platform with credential_fields X-PagerDuty-Api-Key and X-PagerDuty-From-Email, when an admin opens "Connect PagerDuty" from the platform's connector Library, then the rendered credential form shows exactly those two fields and, once saved, the connector detail view lists all 15 tools.
steps: Register the connector on the platform (mcppub register) and have it published to a test tenant's Library
As that tenant, open the Agent platform Library and click the PagerDuty connector card
Read the rendered 'Connect PagerDuty' credential form's field list
Save with placeholder/real credentials and open the connector's detail view
expect: The credential form shows exactly two fields matching X-PagerDuty-Api-Key and X-PagerDuty-From-Email (no extra or missing fields); after saving, the detail view's Tools tab lists 15 tools with an Available badge
notes: Needs a real connector registration and a live platform tenant; not automatable in this repo's own test suite. Not a blocker to development or to reaching 6b/INT (mcp-track.md 2.5/3). Tool count corrected from 14 to 15 to match the as-built tools/list (see docs/tickets/PRD-21237.md Self-test).
